one_sentence: DOI 10.1257/mac.20180090 correctly resolves to Jarociński & Karadi (2020), "Deconstructing Monetary Policy Surprises—The Role of Information Shocks", American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics 12(2): 1-43 — no field mixing, but the title's colon should be an em dash and the author's raw UTF-8 ń should be LaTeX-escaped for BibTeX safety.

issues.original: Deconstructing Monetary Policy Surprises: The Role of Information Shocks
issues.corrected: Deconstructing Monetary Policy Surprises---The Role of Information Shocks
issues.reason: The AEA landing page, the IDEAS/RePEc record (aea/aejmac/v12y2020i2p1-43), and the author's own posted BibTeX all give the title with an em dash separating the two clauses, not a colon. Content and identifiability are unaffected, but the punctuation does not match the canonical title.

issues.original: Jarociński, Marek and Karadi, Peter (raw UTF-8 bytes 0xC5 0x84 for ń)
issues.reason: Spelling and accent placement are correct (ń, n with acute, confirmed against the AEA page and the author's own site jarocinski.github.io) — this is not a name error. But the .bib file embeds the raw UTF-8 character directly rather than a LaTeX-safe escape; under classic (non-8-bit-clean) BibTeX or any non-UTF8 toolchain this can corrupt or crash. authordate3.bst (used by paper_anpec.tex) plus classic bibtex is exactly the fragile combination this affects. The escaped form is safe under bibtex, bibtex8, and biber alike.
Flagged per the audit checklist, but journal-article entries do not require a publisher field under standard .bst styles including authordate3.bst; this is not a defect.
